name: Gideon Spall, Captain of the Last Shift
lore: Gideon Spall was shift-captain on the Crown Drift for twenty years and never lost a man until the deep level broke into the Builders' gallery. He went down first, because a captain goes down first, and he has not come up, because a captain comes up last, and there are still eight of his men in the gallery bringing up ore that is never quite all up. He stands at the deep shift-board with his own token on its hook, counting them past him. Anybody who is not on his board is in the way of the shift.

phases.name: all up
phases.say: He turns from the board and calls the shift by name, all nine, his own last. Down the gallery the baskets stop.

name: Obadiah Fenn, the Receiver of the Struck
lore: Obadiah Fenn received four thousand and eleven struck debtors into the barrow in forty years and entered every one in the register under a number, in a hand the Tallymen called the fairest in the city. In 1019 the post's fees fell owing, the Tallymen struck him off, and nobody came to receive the Receiver. He is still at the register. He has entered himself as four thousand and twelve, and he is waiting for somebody to carry him to his shelf, and he has decided it is you.

phases.name: struck
phases.say: He dips his pen and draws one line across the open register. On every shelf in the barrow something sits up.

name: Magister Ysolde Carrow, the Loud
lore: Ysolde Carrow held the Spire's chair of Saying for eleven years and was put out of it for one lecture, in which she said that the world was dwindling because the Circle had spent a century teaching it to be quiet, and then demonstrated. The Spire's windows on the lake side are still new glass. She took Holmwatch because its Saying-hall carries a voice further than any room the Circle owns, and she Says into it every dusk so that the Toll, the Lamp and the Spire itself will hear that somebody is still speaking up.

phases.name: louder
phases.say: She takes up the great trumpet and Says one word into the brass ribs, and the whole hall rings like the inside of a bell; dust comes down from the vault in a sheet.
